Commentary of Ibn 'Atiyya (al-Muharrar al-Wajiz) on surah 107, verses 1–7:

(p-695) In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

Tafsir of Surah al-Ma'un

It is Meccan without any disagreement that I know of, though al-Tha'labi said it is Medinan.

The Exalted and Majestic said:

﴿Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense?﴾ ﴿For that is the one who repulses the orphan,﴾ ﴿and does not urge the feeding of the needy.﴾ ﴿So woe to those who pray,﴾ ﴿who are heedless of their prayer,﴾ ﴿who make show [of their deeds],﴾ ﴿and withhold [simple] assistance.﴾

This is a warning and an admonition, so that the listener's soul may recall everyone it knows who has this description. Abu 'Amr read "a-ra'ayta" with hamza (according to one transmission from him), while Nafi' and others did not pronounce the hamza. "Al-Din" means the requital, in reward and punishment, and the reckoning here is close to the requital.

Then the Exalted said: ﴿For that is the one who repulses the orphan﴾, meaning: observe in him these evil traits and you will find them. "Da' al-yatim" means pushing him away violently. This may mean: turning him away from feeding him and showing him kindness, or it may mean: depriving him of his right and his property, and this is more severe. Abu Raja' read "yada'u" with a fatha on the dal and a light pronunciation, meaning: he does not show him kindness. The Exalted's words ﴿and does not urge the feeding of the needy﴾ mean: he does not command charity and does not regard it as correct.

It is narrated that this surah was revealed concerning some of those in Mecca who were wavering in Islam, who had not verified it and who were tested and so went astray, and who had this character of rudeness, harshness in dealing with people, and coarseness toward the needy. Perhaps some of them would pray occasionally with the Muslims out of pretence and bewilderment, so Allah the Exalted said concerning them: ﴿So woe to those who pray, who are heedless of their prayer﴾. Ibn Jurayj said: Abu Sufyan used to slaughter a camel every week, and an orphan came to him and he struck him with a stick, so the surah was revealed concerning him. (p-696) Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "I asked the Prophet ﷺ about those who are heedless of their prayer, and he said: 'They are those who delay it beyond its time.'" He means ﷺ, and Allah knows best, the delay of abandonment and neglect. Mujahid inclined to this view. Qatadah said: "Sahun" refers to those who abandon it, or those heedless ones who do not care whether they prayed or did not pray. 'Ata' ibn Yasar said: Praise be to Allah who said "'an salatihim" (from their prayer) and did not say "fi salatihim" (in their prayer). In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud, "lahun" is used instead of "sahun."

The Exalted's words ﴿who make show [of their deeds]﴾ indicate that the prayer of these people is not for Allah the Exalted, is not a clear sign of faith, but is only show before people, so it is not accepted. Ibn Abi Ishaq and Abu al-Ashhab read "yuraw'una" with hamza, short vowel, and a doubled hamza. Ibn Abi Ishaq also transmitted "yura'una" without doubling the hamza.

The Exalted's words ﴿and withhold [simple] assistance﴾ describe them as having little benefit for the servants of Allah, and that is the worst of qualities. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib and Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "al-Ma'un" is zakat. The poet al-Ra'i said:

"A people who in Islam have not withheld their ma'un and have not neglected the tahlil."

(p-697) Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: it is what people lend to one another, such as the axe, the bucket, utensils, scissors and the like. This was also said by al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ibn al-Hanafiyya, Ibn Zayd, al-Dahhak and Ibn 'Abbas. Ibn al-Musayyib said: "al-Ma'un," in the dialect of Quraysh, is wealth. Ibn Mas'ud said: "In the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ we used to reckon al-Ma'un to be the lending of the cooking pot, the bucket and the like."

Tafsir of Surah al-Ma'un

It is Meccan without any disagreement that I know of, though al-Tha'labi said it is Medinan.

The Exalted and Majestic said:

﴿Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense?﴾ ﴿For that is the one who repulses the orphan,﴾ ﴿and does not urge the feeding of the needy.﴾ ﴿So woe to those who pray,﴾ ﴿who are heedless of their prayer,﴾ ﴿who make show [of their deeds],﴾ ﴿and withhold [simple] assistance.﴾

This is a warning and an admonition, so that the listener's soul may recall everyone it knows who has this description. Abu 'Amr read "a-ra'ayta" with hamza (according to one transmission from him), while Nafi' and others did not pronounce the hamza. "Al-Din" means the requital, in reward and punishment, and the reckoning here is close to the requital.

Then the Exalted said: ﴿For that is the one who repulses the orphan﴾, meaning: observe in him these evil traits and you will find them. "Da' al-yatim" means pushing him away violently. This may mean: turning him away from feeding him and showing him kindness, or it may mean: depriving him of his right and his property, and this is more severe. Abu Raja' read "yada'u" with a fatha on the dal and a light pronunciation, meaning: he does not show him kindness. The Exalted's words ﴿and does not urge the feeding of the needy﴾ mean: he does not command charity and does not regard it as correct.

It is narrated that this surah was revealed concerning some of those in Mecca who were wavering in Islam, who had not verified it and who were tested and so went astray, and who had this character of rudeness, harshness in dealing with people, and coarseness toward the needy. Perhaps some of them would pray occasionally with the Muslims out of pretence and bewilderment, so Allah the Exalted said concerning them: ﴿So woe to those who pray, who are heedless of their prayer﴾. Ibn Jurayj said: Abu Sufyan used to slaughter a camel every week, and an orphan came to him and he struck him with a stick, so the surah was revealed concerning him. (p-696) Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "I asked the Prophet ﷺ about those who are heedless of their prayer, and he said: 'They are those who delay it beyond its time.'" He means ﷺ, and Allah knows best, the delay of abandonment and neglect. Mujahid inclined to this view. Qatadah said: "Sahun" refers to those who abandon it, or those heedless ones who do not care whether they prayed or did not pray. 'Ata' ibn Yasar said: Praise be to Allah who said "'an salatihim" (from their prayer) and did not say "fi salatihim" (in their prayer). In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud, "lahun" is used instead of "sahun."

The Exalted's words ﴿who make show [of their deeds]﴾ indicate that the prayer of these people is not for Allah the Exalted, is not a clear sign of faith, but is only show before people, so it is not accepted. Ibn Abi Ishaq and Abu al-Ashhab read "yuraw'una" with hamza, short vowel, and a doubled hamza. Ibn Abi Ishaq also transmitted "yura'una" without doubling the hamza.

The Exalted's words ﴿and withhold [simple] assistance﴾ describe them as having little benefit for the servants of Allah, and that is the worst of qualities. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib and Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "al-Ma'un" is zakat. The poet al-Ra'i said:

"A people who in Islam have not withheld their ma'un and have not neglected the tahlil."

(p-697) Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: it is what people lend to one another, such as the axe, the bucket, utensils, scissors and the like. This was also said by al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ibn al-Hanafiyya, Ibn Zayd, al-Dahhak and Ibn 'Abbas. Ibn al-Musayyib said: "al-Ma'un," in the dialect of Quraysh, is wealth. "The Prophet ﷺ was asked: What is the thing whose withholding is not permitted? He said: 'Water, fire and salt.'" 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, narrated it, and in some routes there is an addition: "and the needle and the leaven." al-Farra' related from some Arabs that al-Ma'un is water. Ibn Mas'ud said: "In the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ we used to reckon al-Ma'un to be the lending of the cooking pot, the bucket and the like."

The tafsir of Surah [al-Ma'un] is complete, and praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
